extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, academics, teachers, and educated generalists
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying the evaluative criteria used by an early-20th-century Nature reviewer to judge scientific books, textbooks, monographs, and natural-history works. The page's guidance covers technical accuracy, pedagogy, illustration/production quality, audience suitability, scholarly apparatus, and ethics in natural-history presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of standard practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a technical work represents 'present standard practice' vs. presenting outdated or non-standard machines (e.g., 'mono-coil-claw' type or certain ironless machines 'are certainly not present standard practice').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books on applied subjects should accurately represent current standard practice; inclusion of non-standard or obscure types should be clearly labelled and justified rather than presented as typical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy of explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness of technical explanations (example: author's explanation why field magnets are laminated is judged 'quite beside the mark').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel or striking explanations must be factually correct; originality is not a defence for demonstrable technical error. Reviewers call out explanations that are 'novel' but incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical recommendation correctness and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether practical recommendations are appropriate and safe for the described context (example: 'indiscriminate recommendation of damping coils' which is 'absolutely harmful' for alternators driven by gas engines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid indiscriminate or context-insensitive recommendations; reviewers expect domain knowledge to flag advice that would be harmful in certain applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and arrangement of archival/correspondence material
rubrics_metrics.description: How the editor selects, sifts, and arranges letters and documentary material (e.g., 'labour of sifting and arranging the correspondence' and the manner the material is dealt with in sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In collected correspondence and memorial volumes, selection must balance representativeness, chronology and thematic grouping so that the material illustrates phases of work and remains usable by readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness / essential omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a memorial or collection covers essential relationships or topics (example: 'the absence of all reference to the relations between Stokes and Lord Kelvin' is noted as an omission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major relationships, collaborations or contextual material should not be omitted in comprehensive memorials; absence of expected material is a notable deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value to experts and novices
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a work is valuable both to specialists ('the most expert craftsman will find much to admire') and to novices ('the novice may derive suggestion and encouragement').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good scholarly works can serve different audiences by preserving deep material for experts while offering insights and encouragement for newcomers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of biographical and ceremonial material
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and treatment of introductory memoirs, personal 'appreciations', and records of celebrations/unveilings ('introductory memoir ... appreciations ... Jubilee celebration ... Westminster Abbey memorial').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical and ceremonial material can add value and context; their inclusion and tasteful handling are part of a successful memorial volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical method effectiveness (teaching by question)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 'teaching by question' and the manner questions are integrated: 'the full advantage of this method cannot be obtained by occasional interpolations of questions ... Such interruptions are apt to be shelved.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises and question-based pedagogy should be integrated coherently with the text (not scattered as intermittent interruptions) to ensure they are actually used by students and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing and progression of instructional content
rubrics_metrics.description: Order in which topics are introduced (example: map scales/directions early but contour-lines not explained until halfway through the book).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructional material should be sequenced so foundational concepts appear before dependent topics; awkward sequencing is a pedagogical fault.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and correct terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy of stated facts and use of correct geographical/historical terminology (examples: county-towns called 'capitals'; coupling of county names; wrong historical statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors of fact and misuse of established terminology are substantive flaws in textbooks and reference works and must be corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and sufficiency of illustrations and views
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and quality of maps, views, and diagrams ('many views and maps', 'needs supplementing with views to enable the child to realise the scenes described').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual material should meaningfully supplement text; in geography and natural history, sufficient and accurate images are essential for comprehension and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and printing quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical production errors in process-illustrations and printing (examples: hemispheres 'not all printed the right way up', phantom coalfield in a figure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful quality control of processed illustrations and printing is required; such production faults materially diminish a work's usefulness and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and balance of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the author keeps an appropriate scope and avoids 'scrappiness' when the subject is vast: 'The immensity of the subject-matter renders occasional "scrappiness" of treatment inevitable, though in general this has been very successfully avoided.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should focus on clear, broad features and contrasts rather than uneven, fragmentary coverage when dealing with vast subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in spelling and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistency in the spelling of place-names (example: Lusern looks out-of-place compared to Torino or Firenze).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent conventions for place-names and specialized terms appropriate to the target audience and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and tone appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of stylistic tone (example: 'enthusiasm for civilisation and progress gives his style a floweriness which is occasionally overdone').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should modulate stylistic flourish to suit the work's purpose and audience; excessive 'floweriness' can detract from scientific clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness for intended audience (schoolbook vs general reading)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the book fits the needs of its intended readership ('not exactly a school-book, should be very useful to teachers'; 'beginners whose homes are in large towns need not be deterred').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define and meet the expectations of the target audience—textbooks should be accessible to students, while treatises may aim at teachers or specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of specific factual claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness of particular etymologies or derivations (example: erroneous derivation of Portland cement from Portland stone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific factual claims must be checked against established knowledge; even small factual errors weaken credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of literature and critical apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and usefulness of literature coverage and critical commentary ('helps but little in the matter of literature ... as a critical guide to the estimation of the various theories his book will be found very useful').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monographs should give adequate literature context; when space prevents exhaustive coverage, the work should still function as a critical guide to arguments and theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to the intended reader's prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of exposition level to readers' background ('the first part is only suitable to the reader who has full acquaintance with the subject or is prepared to look up the literature').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should signal required prior knowledge; sections intended for general readers should avoid assuming specialized background or else provide sufficient explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original contribution and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Author's own additions to the facts and the impartial, searching character of criticism ('Dr. Fitting has himself added materially to the facts ... opinions ... extremely valuable ... searching but unbiased critic').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valuable scholarly work both contributes original observations/experiments and applies impartial, critical assessment to competing theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical methods and authenticity in natural-history illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical approach to natural-history material and authenticity of images ('To take birds' nests and their contents with the camera is ... more satisfactory than egg-collecting'; '"faked" photographs are thoroughly unsatisfactory').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer non-destructive, ethical methods (photography over collecting); authenticity matters—staged or 'faked' images of specimens are criticised as unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical field-utility for beginners
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a field guide or natural-history book is practically useful for beginners in local contexts ('nests ... observed within a radius of sixteen miles ... beginners ... need not be deterred').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guides should indicate the accessibility of field observations and encourage beginners by showing achievable scope and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly rigor: evidence separation, terminology, and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which an author separates 'the attested from the doubtful', recommends improved terminology ('matrilocal instead of heena'), and provides a helpful index ('There is an excellent index').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good scholarship distinguishes reliable facts from doubtful reports, proposes clear, adoptable terminology, and supplies a usable index/bibliography to aid future study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of argumentation and reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Tightness and persuasiveness of arguments ('the argument is closely reasoned').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly claims should be supported by closely reasoned argumentation; this is especially important in theoretical discussions (e.g., group marriage, kinship evolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness as textbook or reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the work can serve as a textbook or indispensable reference ('will be indispensable to anthropologists, and sociologists generally will find it an admirable and convenient text-book').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works and textbooks should be organized, indexed, and balanced so that they can be adopted as standard resources by specialists and instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography and referencing completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and adequacy of bibliographic apparatus (example: 'finally, there is a Bibliography of fifteen pages').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of a substantive bibliography is an important scholarly feature, enabling readers to follow up primary sources and situate arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and soundness of philosophical/theoretical argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity, avoidance of vagueness, and navigating between extremes in philosophical discussion ('a few passages either vague or disputable' ; 'sensibly steers a middle course between the extremes of pure empiricism and the a priori hypothesis').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical and theoretical works should aim for clear exposition, avoid unnecessary vagueness, and justify their position in relation to opposing views.
